Fixed the actual blocker: GitHub had a corrupted committed `debug.keystore`, so release packaging failed after compilation.

Changes applied:
- Release QA now uses Android’s generated debug signer instead of the broken tracked keystore.
- CI explicitly creates and validates a fresh QA signing key before building.
- Clarified in code: these APKs are **QA-signed**, not Play Store production-signed.

Validation so far:
- TypeScript: passed.
- Expo tests: **1085 passed, 0 failed**.
- Gradle signing configuration: passed; release correctly resolves the generated QA signer.
- Full local APK build exceeds this sandbox’s 60-second command limit, but it progressed through compilation without the previous keystore error.

The next GitHub emulator run will perform the full build, install, launch, Maestro test, screenshots, and artifact upload. I will not call the APK verified until that run is green.
